newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ILLOVO , TONGAAT STRIKE ENTERS THIRD DAY.
newsitem.headline: ILLOVO , TONGAAT STRIKE ENTERS THIRD DAY.

text.p: A three-day-old wage strike in South Africa's sugar milling and refining industry by 4,000 workers, shows no signs of being resolved, worker and employer officials said on Friday.
Workers at 14 mills and refineries belonging to Illovo Sugar Ltd and Tongaat-Hulett Ltd have downed tools to back their demands of a 20 percent wage increase across the board.
Food and Allied Workers' Union spokesman Zwile Zulu said there were no negotiations between employers and the five unions representing the striking workers.

"Since the strike started (on Tuesday night) there have been no real negotiations to end the strike. (The employers) are not convinced that we have genuine problems with their wage offer," Zulu told Reuters.
"There has been no need for us to approach them...they know that our demands are not rigid, we are flexible," he added.
Zulu said the striking unions were demanding a 20 percent wage hike to narrow a 40 percent gap between what sugar workers were earning compared to other workers in the food and beverage sector.
On average sugar workers earn about 1,300 rand a month, he said.
The official spokesman representing both Illovo and Tongaat-Hulett could not be reached for comment.
A sugar industry source, who declined to be named, said production of about 83,500 tons of cane per day was being lost, but declined to put a value on the figure.
Growers had been warned of the strike and advised to not cut their cane until the strike was resolved, the source said.

"If this strike can be resolved by Monday it is felt the loss in production can be made up in the rest of the season. If there is no result on Monday there will be a release of more information," the source said.
The harvesting season began in April and ends in December.
The current season's production has been estimated at 2.5 million tons with 48 percent being exported for the 1997/98 season rising from 44 percent in the 1996/97 period.
Overall exports earnings are expected to be 1,462 billion rand which was an increase of 271 million rand over last season.
